newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa board details expected maize pool prices.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa board details expected maize pool prices.

text.p: South Africa's Maize Board on Friday announced the expected target prices for maize delivered into its export pools during the 1996/97 season.
Vic Mouton, the board's chairman said in a statement target prices on white maize in pools one, two and three were 580, 570 and 520 rand a tonne respectively.
He said interim payments of respectively 63, 61 and 55 rand at tonne were being made on this maize.
For yellow maize prices had been set at 670, 645 and 525 with interim payments at 21, 35 and 57 respectively.

Mouton said interim payments of 120 rand a tonne and 100 rand had already been made on yellow maize in pools one and two. He said final payments for all pools would take place once pools were finalised at the end of the season on April 30.
He said virtually all the maize received was sold and prices were based on ruling circumstances experienced in the market.
"The target prices, therefore, reflect the yields obtained, but elements such as changes in the rate of exchange and in the rate of interest may result in deviations," he said.
South Africa's export maize market has been partially deregulated with private traders active alongside the state-owned Maize Board which invites maize for a number of export pools it runs.
From May 1, the Maize Board will cease to play a role in the market altogether.

Pools close and a new one is opened once a certain quantity of maize or a time limit is reached. Although pools this year were designated for export maize, the board did sell some maize locally on tender following fears of a domestic shortage.
